mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen for three consecutive weeks (-4.3, -9.6, -17.3) before a slight partial rebound (-14.4). Absent new shocks, mobility series exhibit autocorrelated momentum, so the recent deceleration in decline will persist and compound into a further mild decline over the next four weeks as households continue consolidating non-essential trips.
evidence_refs: fact:three consecutive weekly declines in RETAIL_REC followed by partial rebound at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, indicating momentum did not carry through.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week collapse in TRANSIT (from -4.1 to -21.3 over three weeks) reflects commuter and leisure-trip avoidance of crowded transit. When TRANSIT drops more than 20 points below baseline, substitution away from transit-dependent retail destinations intensifies, suppressing RETAIL_REC further over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 20 points from baseline in the latest week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -21.3 and -20.7 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT remaining below -20 points.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL (1.0 to 6.3) and decline in WORKPLACES (-0.7 to -7.7) jointly indicate a structural shift toward staying home for both work and leisure. When these two series move in opposite directions together, the combined stay-home effect compounds to depress RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict, over a four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 1.0 to 6.3 while WORKPLACES fell from -0.7 to -7.7 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES stays suppressed, breaking the joint co-movement linkage.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS decline in t-1w (-18.9) followed by partial recovery to -5.3 suggests intermittent outdoor-activity restrictions consistent with a tightening-restrictions regime. Under such a regime, any residual retail footfall tied to outdoor leisure trips will continue to be constrained, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -18.9 then partially recovered to -5.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks despite PARKS remaining depressed below -10, indicating the restriction-linkage mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: Early-to-mid March in Tokyo coincides with pre-spring seasonal outdoor activity increases (e.g., cherry blossom anticipation). The partial PARKS rebound from -18.9 to -5.3 may reflect this seasonal pull overriding restriction effects. If PARKS continues rising past a +10 point threshold, associated foot traffic will spill over into nearby retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above +10 points from baseline in a subsequent week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded from -18.9 to -5.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: PARKS crosses above +10 but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises without any PARKS threshold crossing.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained near baseline (2.1, 6.6, 0.0, 0.3) despite large swings in other categories, indicating essential-trip behavior is decoupled from discretionary retail. This stability signals no panic-buying or hoarding wave is underway, so short-term RETAIL_REC movement will be driven by other factors rather than essential-goods substitution, implying no independent lift from GROCERY_PHARM over the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within a narrow -0 to +7 point band across four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM spikes sharply (e.g., beyond +15 points) and RETAIL_REC rises in tandem within one week, contradicting the decoupling assumption.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES decline together week-on-week (as seen from t-2w to t-0w, TRANSIT -17.0 to -20.7 and WORKPLACES -10.1 to -7.7 with lag), this joint suppression signals active government or employer-driven social distancing policy. In a tightening-restrictions regime, this combination compounds to suppress discretionary retail visits more than transit or workplace declines alone, extending the RETAIL_REC decline over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show deep negative values across the snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days even while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain deeply negative, indicating the joint-policy mechanism is not operative.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC decline decelerated from -17.3 to -14.4 in the most recent week, the first improvement after three weeks of worsening. If this deceleration exceeds a 2-point threshold improvement, it signals an inflection point where the public is adapting to the new normal and resuming some discretionary trips, leading to a net positive shift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week change improves by more than 2 points after prior declines
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -17.3 to -14.4, a 2.9 point week-on-week gain
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC resumes its decline in the following weeks despite the observed one-week deceleration, falling below -14.4 on average over the next 28 days.
